questions: Does max_error fall below 0.055 m on the oval and s-bend, and which track still ends first?
Does steering_oscillation rise above 0.1? If so, is it the forward lead or the narrower track?
Is line_loss_events still 0 with the sensors at y = 0.07 m?
What is progress per track, and does any run exceed 0.5?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If steering_oscillation exceeds 0.1 with max_error unchanged, return sensor y to 0.05 m and keep wheel_track 0.09 m. If max_error falls but the robot still leaves the track, try wheel_track 0.08 m.

intent: Test whether more forward sensor lead (y 0.04 to 0.07 m) plus more turn authority (wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 m) reduces max_error below the 0.06 m off-track limit, while keeping the zero-line-loss sensing layout. The body inertia change from iteration 2 is kept so this race isolates lead and turn authority.
learning: Iterations 1 and 2 show that sensor footprint and body inertia barely move max_error (0.060 to 0.061 m), so the next lever is sensor lead and turn authority. Measure max_error and progress per track against the 0.06 m limit.
rationale: Iteration 2 (26.6355) was effectively unchanged from iteration 1 (26.6434). Lighter mass and shorter body with a narrower track (0.10 m) left max_error at about 0.061 m, progress at 0.04 to 0.115, and steering oscillation at about 0.07. Iteration 1 had already removed line loss, and the body-inertia change did not reduce drift. So neither the sensor footprint nor yaw inertia is the limit. Every run still leaves the 0.06 m band with the line still under the sensors, which points to the response being too late. The sensors sit only 0.04 m ahead of the axle, so the controller sees a bend only about 4 cm before the wheels reach it. Next I move the sensor row forward to y = 0.07 m, which gives roughly 3 cm more lead on each bend. I keep the spread at +/-0.05 m and the 16 mm footprint, which gave zero line loss. I also return wheel_track to 0.09 m, the Integrator's suggested step for more turn authority, while keeping mass 0.5 kg and body_length 0.12 m. Expected result: max_error falls below about 0.05 m on the oval and s-bend, progress rises above 0.2, and line_loss_events stays at 0. Risk: a 0.07 m lead plus a narrower track may increase oscillation above 0.1, which would point to the lead being too aggressive.
